tagline: Above the river canyon, through cattlemen’s summer country.
intro: Near North Fork, Minarets Road climbs above the San Joaquin River canyon toward Mile High Vista, then descends toward Mammoth Pool Reservoir. The byway continues through the high meadows on Beasore Road before turning toward Cold Springs Summit and the descent to Highway 41 near Oakhurst.

These roads began with work to do. Beasore Road follows the old routes for moving cattle to summer range, and Minarets Road grew with the Mammoth Pool hydroelectric project. It was also meant to cross the Sierra to Mammoth Lakes. A 1957 federal study found that feasible, and it was never built.

moments.title: Mile High Vista
moments.text: From Mile High Vista the view runs over the San Joaquin River canyon and Mammoth Pool Reservoir to the Minarets and Mount Ritter.

moments.title: Beasore Meadows
moments.text: At Beasore Meadows, Jones Store historically served cattlemen moving livestock between the San Joaquin Valley and summer grazing ground.

moments.title: Cold Springs Summit
moments.text: At 7,308 feet the summit is the highest point on the byway, and a short trail leads to Cold Springs Meadow with views toward Madera Peak.

practical: High-elevation sections are not plowed in winter; the usual driving season is June through October, depending on snow and road conditions.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Sierra National Forest scenic drives
